title: Reconcile OpenSSL ABI/soname drift and modernize OAuth/JWT/SAML stacks across platform services
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Over the last 18 months several services in the runtime plane and auth layer drifted onto different SSL/JWT/SAML library versions. This has produced intermittent TLS handshake failures (symbol mismatch on alpine-edge images), inconsistent JWK parsing between services, and high-friction SSO support for enterprise customers using older IdPs. In addition, we need to align to our supply-chain policy (minimum OpenSSL 3.x, vetted JWT library versions) and reduce patch churn.

Scope: This ticket consolidates the following work across multiple services: (1) standardize system OpenSSL to 3.0.11+ on our base images and ensure the runtime components (C++ runtime, go-proxy, and python auth service) link against the same SONAME; (2) migrate platform auth services from an unmaintained JWT helper to Nimbus JOSE+JWT (Java) / Authlib (Python) / golang-jwt v5; (3) replace legacy SAML XML parser used in the idp-adapter with a memory-safe parser and add strict canonicalization checks; (4) add CI smoke tests and runtime assertions to detect ABI mismatches during image builds.

Goals and success criteria:
- No TLS handshake symbol mismatches on our base Ubuntu/Alpine builds or on Dedicated customer images.
- All core services pass the newly added TLS/JWK compatibility matrix in CI within 6 runs.
- Vulnerable transitive OpenSSL references eliminated (scan reports 0 critical/1 high allowed) and documented exceptions approved.
- Zero regression in SSO flows for 3 enterprise test IdPs and <1% error increase in production auth requests during rollout window.

Non-goals: Removing support for customers on legacy cipher suites (that is a separate compatibility program), rewriting the entire auth stack, or introducing a new PKCS#11 provider in this ticket.

Approach:
1) Inventory and pin: run an automated license/soname inventory across images (artifact: https://drive.redwood.com/rd-open/dep-inventory-2026-03-01). Produce a matrix of actual libssl.so.* references per image.
2) Build standardized base images: create openssl-3.0.11 builds (Ubuntu 22.04 and alpine-3.19 compat layer) and ship to our internal registry behind a feature flag.
3) Library migration: incrementally modify consumers to use target JWT/SAML libraries with compatibility shims in a shared auth-common repo (Java/Python/Go shims exposing uniform JWK parsing API).
4) CI & smoke tests: add a matrix job that rebuilds images and runs handshake tests against test IdPs and a mutual-tls echo service. Block merges on failures for 72 hours after the first discovery of a new symbol.
5) Rolling deployment: Canary on non-customer critical clusters for 48h, then staggered rollout to production traffic routes with a kill-switch to rollback to previous images if auth error rate exceeds threshold.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We chose to standardize on OpenSSL 3.0.x instead of immediately moving to 3.1 to reduce kernel/packaging risk; 3.0 is supported by our key cloud images and has long-term patches.
- For Java we selected Nimbus JOSE+JWT for its active maintenance, but we will keep our own thin compatibility wrapper to avoid API churn for callers.
- Alpine compatibility requires a small shim for BN/CT functions; that shim is implemented as a static symbol alias layer to avoid wholesale rebuilds of all transitive deps.
- There is a short-term perf cost in the shim layer (~2-3% CPU for TLS handshakes in microbenchmarks) which we will monitor; if unacceptable we will prioritize a rebuild path for a small set of latency-sensitive binaries.

Testing and validation:
- Unit and integration tests for new JWT parsing behavior (edge cases: kid-less JWKs, exp/nbf fuzzy windows, critical headers).
- SAML end-to-end tests with three IdPs (Okta, ADFS, PingFederate) and a synthetic SAML breaker that injects malformed canonicalization to validate robustness.
- Load tests on canary cluster verifying <5% increase in 95th-percentile auth latency.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (this ticket): Inventory + base-image builds pushed to registry (feature flag off).
- Week 2: Implement auth-common shims and migrate 4 low-risk services (auth-proxy, idp-adapter, metrics-ingest-auth, grpc-auth).
- Week 3: CI smoke matrix live; canary rollout to staging and non-customer clusters.
- Week 4: Production canary and staged rollout; monitor for 72h.

Rollback and mitigation:
- Each image build has a pinned previous image tag; if error rates exceed 1.5x baseline we will rollback the release route-by-route.
- If unexpected JWK parsing behavior appears, the auth-common shim can be toggled (feature flag) to use legacy parser for that service while a patch is produced.

Artifacts and links:
- Dep inventory: https://drive.redwood.com/rd-open/dep-inventory-2026-03-01
- RFC: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/OpenSSL+Consolidation+RFC
- Draft PR (auth-common): https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-common/pull/334
- Build job: https://ci.redwood.com/jenkins/job/openssl-3x-base

Open questions:
- Do we require FIPS-mode builds for Dedicated customers in this ticket or handle as a follow-up? (Security/Compliance asked to decide by 2026-03-10).
- Are there any platform teams that explicitly need older ciphers we must preserve? Please call them out so we can add compatibility lanes.
